paper_metadata.title: Bermudan option pricing by quantum amplitude estimation and Chebyshev interpolation

experiments.description: Proposed quantum Bermudan option pricing algorithm using Chebyshev interpolation for continuation values and quantum amplitude estimation to estimate continuation values at Chebyshev nodes, with a final QAE step for the present option price.

algorithm.variant: Chebyshev interpolation + quantum amplitude estimation for Bermudan option pricing

hyperparameters.mk: degree of Chebyshev polynomials for each exercise date k
hyperparameters.NQAE_k: QAE iteration number for each k in [K-1]0
hyperparameters.Nrep_k: number of QAE repetitions for each k in [K-1]0
hyperparameters.eVmax_k: upper bound on |G_k[\hat V_k](s)| for each k
hyperparameters.Dk: hyper-rectangle [L1,k,U1,k] x ... x [Ld,k,Ud,k] for each k
hyperparameters.rho_k: Bernstein ellipse parameter for analyticity assumption
hyperparameters.B_k: analytic bound on Q_k over Bernstein ellipse
hyperparameters.epsilon_QAE_k: QAE estimation error parameter at each node

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Underlying asset path distribution is encoded in a quantum state via O_step,k; payoff/continuation value is scaled into [0,1] and encoded into a single-qubit rotation for QAE.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate Bermudan option price V0 = sup_{tau in T} E[f_pay_tau(S_tau)] by backward dynamic programming with V_k(s) = max(f_pay_k(s), Q_k(s)) and Q_k(s) = E[V_{k+1}(S_{k+1}) | S_k = s].
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: No explicit constraints beyond the stopping-time dynamic programming structure; out-of-domain asset values handled by either known outside-bound approximation V_OB_k or flat extrapolation F_k.

problem_instance.description: General Bermudan option pricing problem with d underlying assets and K exercise dates; no single numerical benchmark instance is reported.

dataset_specification.description: General Markov process model for underlying asset prices; examples discussed include basket put options under models such as Black-Scholes, but no concrete dataset or market ticker set is evaluated.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Underlying asset evolution is assumed to be generated by a quantum oracle O_step,k, typically corresponding to a discretized SDE simulation such as Euler-Maruyama; continuous distributions are discretized as needed.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: The paper provides theoretical error bounds and complexity analysis only; no numerical experiments, benchmark tables, or empirical runs are reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Chebyshev interpolation coefficients are computed from QAE-estimated nodal continuation values; values outside interpolation domains are handled by V_OB_k or flat extrapolation.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Final option price is recovered from the QAE-estimated probability via (2P0 - 1) eVmax_1.

speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical Monte Carlo-based methods such as least-squares Monte Carlo
speedup_claims.conditions: assuming access to the required quantum oracles and that QAE succeeds; asymptotic scaling in error tolerance epsilon
speedup_claims.caveats: The claimed oracle-call complexity is O~(epsilon^-1 log^d(epsilon^-1) polyloglog(epsilon^-1)), so the quadratic improvement is in epsilon only and includes logarithmic factors; no numerical experiment is reported.
The paper cites the standard QAE advantage of O(epsilon^-1) versus O(epsilon^-2) sampling.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O~(epsilon^-1 log^d(epsilon^-1) polyloglog(epsilon^-1)) oracle calls to O_step,k
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O~(epsilon^-2) oracle/sample calls for Monte Carlo-based methods such as LSM
